disease_label_per_paper: Recurrent (right) tubal ectopic pregnancy after prior contralateral salpingectomy, unruptured, initial beta-hCG > 5,000 IU/L, managed conservatively with repeated methotrexate
presentation_summary: 30-year-old nulliparous woman (G4P0) with an 8-day history of right-sided lower abdominal pain and mild vaginal spotting; last menstrual period 8 weeks prior; history of left salpingectomy for tubal ectopic pregnancy 3 years earlier; no PID, IUD or ART; non-smoker.

Admission vitals: BP 109/70 mmHg, HR 81/min, RR 20/min, T 36.2 C. Abdomen soft without guarding or rebound; slight bleeding from the uterine cavity; no cervical motion pain; uterus normal size, non-tender; right adnexa thickened, non-tender.

Transvaginal ultrasound: no intrauterine gestational sac (endometrium 10.4 mm); 13 x 10 mm mixed-echo lesion adjacent to the right ovary with a small hypoechoic area and abundant peripheral flow; possible corpus luteum 18 x 12 mm in right ovary (O-RADS 2); no pelvic free fluid.
Labs: serum beta-hCG 5,823 IU/L; Hb 119 g/L; ALT 10.6 U/L, AST 17 U/L; renal function and coagulation normal.
